checks.title: Self hosted platform detected
checks.rationale: Coolify and Dokploy change what a safe host looks like: they publish a reverse proxy and a panel, write app .env files on every deploy and keep the SSH keys of every server they manage. Knowing the platform and its role (panel or managed server) tells the other checks what to expect. Without Docker facts the role and version come from the disk only and may stay unknown.
checks.fix: Nothing to fix; this records the platform for the other checks.

checks.title: Platform proxy is not published on all interfaces behind a tunnel
checks.rationale: When a tunnel is meant to be the only way in, a proxy published on 0.0.0.0 lets anyone who finds the origin IP skip the tunnel and with it the WAF, access policies and rate limits. Docker publishes past UFW, so a UFW input rule is not proof the port is closed; only the DOCKER-USER chain (or ufw-docker, which hooks into it) filters it. A proxy the chain drops for every outside source is a warning, not a failure: it is filtered today but one firewall change from public, so publish it on 127.0.0.1. On a public web host, ports beyond 80 and 443 (such as the Traefik dashboard on 8080) should never be published. A panel host whose proxy is public on 80 and 443 is inferred as paas-panel, even with a tunnel beside it: the proxy serves the panel's certificates and every app it deploys. Then the proxy passes, or is info when a tunnel runs too, as a reminder to publish it on 127.0.0.1 and pass --profile tunnel if the tunnel is meant to be the only way in.
checks.fix: Publish the proxy on 127.0.0.1 only (for example 127.0.0.1:443:443) when ingress is a tunnel; never publish the Traefik dashboard or enable api.insecure.
checks.breaks: Anything reaching the proxy directly by IP stops working; check the tunnel serves every hostname first.

checks.title: Platform panel ports are not open to the world
checks.rationale: The Coolify panel (8000, plus 6001 and 6002 for realtime and terminal) and the Dokploy panel (3000) grant root on every managed server to whoever logs in, and an unclaimed fresh install lets the first visitor create the admin account. Published Docker ports bypass UFW, so a wildcard listener is reachable unless the Docker chain filters it.
checks.fix: Reach the panel over the tailnet or behind an access proxy, and publish its ports on 127.0.0.1 or the tailnet address.
checks.breaks: Losing the only path to the panel locks you out of it; keep a tailnet path working before closing the public one.

checks.title: No platform database is published publicly
checks.rationale: Both platforms offer a "publicly available" switch on databases that publishes the port on every interface. Docker publishes past UFW, so the database is open to the internet and to password guessing and known exploits. A DOCKER-USER rule that drops unknown sources turns the failure into a warning: the port is still published and one rule change away from public.
checks.verify: docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Image}} {{.Ports}}' | grep -Ei 'postgres|mysql|maria|mongo|redis|valkey|clickhouse'; sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER
checks.fix: Turn off "publicly available" for the database and reach it over the tailnet or an SSH tunnel.
checks.breaks: Clients that connect over the public port lose access until they use the private path.

checks.title: Projects do not share the platform default network
checks.rationale: Coolify attaches apps to its "coolify" destination network and Dokploy to "dokploy-network" unless a project gets its own. On a shared network every app resolves and reaches every other project's services by name, including databases, so one compromised app can talk to the rest. DKR-030 judges every network; this check names the platform setting behind it.
checks.fix: Give each project its own destination (Coolify: a new destination network per project; Dokploy: an isolated network per compose project) and attach the platform proxy to each.
checks.breaks: Apps that call another project's service by its container name stop resolving it; route those calls through the proxy or join only the two that need it.

checks.title: Docker Swarm ports are restricted to cluster peers
checks.rationale: Dokploy runs on Docker Swarm. The swarm management port 2377/tcp, node gossip on 7946/tcp and udp, and the VXLAN overlay on 4789/udp must only be reachable by other cluster nodes: an open management port or overlay lets outsiders talk to the cluster control plane or inject overlay traffic.
checks.fix: Allow 2377/tcp, 7946/tcp and udp and 4789/udp only from the other nodes' addresses (or the tailnet), deny them from anywhere else.
checks.breaks: Blocking a real peer splits the swarm; list every node before narrowing the rules.
